cases.hypothesis: A trailing plus operator in arithmetic or JavaScript coercion text expects another operand.
positive_cues: Final token is a plus sign in each example
Arithmetic expressions and sums are being continued
JavaScript unary-plus coercion syntax is shown
exclusion_cues: Ordinary prose with no operator continuation
Phone-number digits interpreted without mathematical context

cases.hypothesis: A subject clause requiring a negative predicate expressing inability, exclusion, or unusability.
positive_cues: Administration is expected to be unable to fix the problem
We and you introduce cannot-style predicates
Printer is described as unusable or incompatible
exclusion_cues: Standalone noun completion without a following predicate

cases.hypothesis: References to Microsoft as a company and software-platform ecosystem.
positive_cues: Microsoft is explicitly repeated across all contexts
MSN.com and Skype are named Microsoft services
Graph API, Intune, and Windows Runtime are Microsoft technologies
exclusion_cues: Non-Microsoft companies or unrelated software ecosystems
Generic technology mentions without a Microsoft entity

cases.hypothesis: Health-care professional or provider terminology in medical and nursing text.
positive_cues: Qualified healthcare professional completes a medical disclaimer
Other health professionals appear in care referrals
Health professional and health care professionals recur in clinical literature
exclusion_cues: Nonmedical uses of health without a care provider
General business or legal text lacking clinical context

cases.hypothesis: Legal citation attribution naming counsel or parties after the word 'for'.
positive_cues: All contexts are formal judicial case records
Attorney-for and counsel-for boilerplate is repeated
Plaintiff, appellant, and plaintiffs in error follow legal attributions
exclusion_cues: Everyday prepositional uses of 'for' outside legal filings
Nonlegal text without attorneys or listed parties
